Independent derivative, threshold and lattice replay
correctness.rationale: For the corrected record, the fixed-initial-abundance hazard gives expected survivors N exp(−Td₀) Σᵢ exp(−a/(b+rᵢ)), a=Td₁N>0, with zero survival at zero total cover. The simplex is compact and the zero-cover extension is continuous. With pair total cover C fixed and x<C/2, the derivative of the pair objective has the sign of H(x/C)−a/C. Writing y=(C−x)/x>1 gives H=2y log(y)/(y²−1), strictly increasing in x/C from 0 to 1: log(y)−(y²−1)/(y²+1) is positive by differentiation from y=1. Thus an unequal interior pair is strictly below an endpoint or the midpoint on its feasible interval; every maximizing allocation has j equal positive supplements R/j, with arbitrary occupied labels. After dropping the common baseline and prefactor, the support objective is Qⱼ=j[exp(−θuⱼ)−exp(−θv)] for β=b/R>0, θ=a/R, uⱼ=j/(1+βj), v=1/β. Qⱼ₊₁/Qⱼ is (j+1)/j times the upper-tail probability of [uⱼ₊₁,v] under density proportional to exp(−θt) on [uⱼ,v]. This decreases strictly by exponential tilting, starts above 1 at θ↓0 by the interval lengths, and tends to 0. Hence each adjacent equality occurs once. For continuous support x>0, Q′ has the sign of 1/λ−L(z), where λ=θ/β, z=λ/(1+βx), and L(z)=∫₀¹(1−s)exp(−zs)ds. L increases strictly as x increases, to 1/2. The derivative is strictly positive when λ≤2; when λ>2 it changes sign once from positive to negative since L(λ)<1/λ. Consequently at an adjacent equality exactly those two integers are global maximizers. At θⱼ the next larger support is already worse than j+1, and the next smaller is already worse than j; the strict ratio monotonicity orders their crossings θⱼ₊₁<θⱼ<θⱼ₋₁ wherever defined. Thus the staircase has no skips or extra tie sizes. At β=0 the objective becomes j exp(−θj); its adjacent ratios give ordered crossings log((j+1)/j). Bracketing the positive-baseline root with points on either side of the zero-baseline crossing proves convergence as β↓0. The independent replay reproduced the four-patch β=1/2 crossing values 1.358513260963, 1.496945595991 and 1.828133590308 and the strict support-2 optimum at θ=1.6. The 20,460 simplex-lattice comparisons had no discrepancy beyond roundoff (maximum excess 5.55e−17). Reading the bundled checker and recomputing loop counts gives 1,632, 523,590, 56,000, 119,988, 552 and 614,215 diagnostics, totaling 1,315,977; the first count denotes support values across 136 exact tie cases.
residual_risks: The independent decimal thresholds and lattice replay are bounded floating-point checks, not a proof for real-valued allocations or arbitrary parameters. The bundled checker was not executed during the review.

The result assumes identical patches, fixed total supplement, and a hazard evaluated at initial abundance throughout the exposure. It does not apply as stated to dynamic depletion or heterogeneous patches.

evidence: Ginsberg is the strongest identified plausible general comparator, but full text was not obtained; the Case PDF for Vicentini returned HTTP 403.
Samhouri et al. Eq. (1) gives the additive refuge hazard. Its field application uses an ODE with changing prey abundance and found better support for the piecewise alternative.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general optimization algorithm at fixed parameter values is not by itself a theorem on strict crossing order as the hazard parameter varies. The biological antecedent provides the hazard, not a supplementary-cover allocation theorem; its dynamic application is not equivalent to the fixed-hazard objective.

evidence: The prey occupancy proof uses rational-product thresholds, not ratios of integrals over nested intervals with exponential tilts. The Hill proof uses a fixed peak of benefit per dose; applying a nonlinear change to identify the returns would not preserve the linear total-supplement constraint.
Even a prior reduction to equal positive allocations would leave adjacent equalities to locate and order. The explicit tilt and strict continuous-support unimodality give these steps here.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The inspected staircase proofs and hazard equation do not imply the positive-baseline ordered crossings. A full prior identical-plant result that supplies these order and equality conclusions for this family would change the assessment; the accessible excerpt does not establish that implication.
searches: Full Resultary prey occupancy and Hill active-target proofs; Samhouri et al. Eq. (1); publisher excerpt of Ginsberg's identical-plant solution

evidence: The problem is exactly a separable fixed-sum allocation with common return exp(−a/(b+r))−exp(−a/b), up to constants and a positive multiplier. This is an identical-plant problem; the return can have one inflection, changing from convex to concave at total cover a/2.

Vicentini's abstract addresses S-shaped allocation, and Ginsberg's publisher excerpt claims a complete solution of the identical-plant problem. Only those accessible materials were read for these two works.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A prior identical-plant theorem can cover optimizer structure without using refuge terminology. Neither accessible text supplies an evaluated shifted exponential crossing law or proves that varying θ visits every support in order. Whether their full results imply more remains open in this review.
searches: Public literature on fixed-sum S-shaped resource allocation and identical-plant allocation: Vicentini (1970), Case operations report 370; Ginsberg (1974), DOI 10.1016/0022-0531(74)90053-2

evidence: The prey occupancy staircase allocates biomass with return rt−(r/K)t²−ct/(1+ht). Its adjacent differences are affine in c and give rational-product thresholds, unlike the exponential-tail equations here.
The Hill staircase uses log(1+xʰ), with a fixed benefit-per-dose peak and a varying budget. It is not a table of positive-baseline refuge thresholds.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: A prior support table with the same objective and crossing parameter would suffice even under different terminology. These two full records enumerate different objectives; matching the qualitative staircase does not make either threshold table equivalent.
searches: Resultary refuge/shelter and allocation-staircase comparisons; full prey occupancy staircase 0d3ae31b84de and Hill active-target staircase a81be9bbd6bd

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge pass for the explicit shifted inverse-exponential support selector with strictly ordered positive-baseline crossings and exact ties, not for S-shaped resource allocation, the hazard model or the general idea of a staircase. General identical-plant allocation is a real equivalence risk: the available historical abstracts could cover the structural reduction, but they do not establish the particular parameter-dependent crossing and no-skip theorem. This is not a claim of exhaustive priority.
residual_risks: The complete texts of Vicentini (1970) and Ginsberg (1974) were not obtained. Their accessible material cannot settle priority for the equal-positive reduction or exclude a general theorem that implies more.
Search coverage is not exhaustive. The originality assessment is for the ordered positive-baseline selector and tie classification as a whole.

Full prey occupancy and Hill staircase comparators
value.rationale: For a fixed supplement across identical patches, the theorem determines exactly when to spread protection and when to concentrate it as the held hazard increases. Every support size occurs on a nonempty interval, and baseline-dependent thresholds distinguish equal-support ties from regimes with a single maximizing support size. The result is an exact benchmark with a transparent scope, beyond the existence of an allocation rule or a finite numerical example.
residual_risks: The benchmark does not justify field recommendations, fitted parameter thresholds, or extrapolation to changing prey abundances and heterogeneous patches.
